traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants annual or perennial; FOC herbs perennial or annual.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants deciduous, usually forming over-wintering buds (hibernaculae).

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): Drosera: lateral circinate or scorpioid cymes.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): Drosera's inflorescences lateral.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals (4 or) 5 (or 6-12); petals 5.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 5, usually joined at the base; FOC as many as the petals.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): gynoecium 3-carpellate; FOC 2-5-carpellate.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals and petals 5, free or joined at the base.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals persistent; petals too persistent, closing and twisting after flowering.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsules splitting between the placentae.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsules obovoid.

traits.capsule_valves.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsule dehiscent, 2-6-valved; FNA 3 carpels.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blades unlobed.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blades unlobed: suborbiculate, orbiculate, spatulate, obovate, cuneate to linear.

rules.appearance.stem_hairs.glands.densi.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera rotundifolia, D. anglica and D. filiformis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes glabrous.

rules.appearance.stem_hairs.glands.count.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Drosera rotundifolia, D. anglica and D. filiformis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes glabrous.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.hairs_benea.note: Darwin, Insectivorous Plants (1875), p.4: 'The whole upper surface is covered with gland-bearing filaments'; p.8: the lower surface bears only minute non-secreting papillae.

rules.appearance.organs.basal.hairs_bene.note: Darwin, Insectivorous Plants (1875), p.4 and p.8, as for the stem leaves: tentacles on the upper surface only.

appearance.stem_hairs.glands.density.why: A sundew's scape is bare: its tentacles stand on its blades alone.

appearance.stem_hairs.glands.count.why: A sundew's counted tentacles are its blades', none on its scape.

appearance.organs.leaf.hairs_beneath.gla.why: A sundew's tentacles stand on the blade's upper face and rim; its underside has none.

appearance.organs.basal.hairs_beneath.gl.why: A sundew's tentacles stand on the blade's upper face and rim; its underside has none.
